prompt.text: Which is not a tenet of cell theory?

options: All living things are composed of one or more cells
The cell is the basic unit of life
New cells arise from existing ones
questions.explanation: Cell theory states organisms are made of cells, the cell is the basic unit of life, and cells come from preexisting cells—not that cells require water as a tenet.

prompt.text: True or false: Prokaryotes do not have membrane-bound organelles.

questions.explanation: Prokaryotes lack membrane-bound organelles (no nucleus, mitochondria, etc.).

prompt.text: Archaea is a domain that exclusively contains:

questions.explanation: Archaea are prokaryotes (no nucleus), forming their own domain.

prompt.text: The ability of the cell membrane to allow some molecules to enter or leave while blocking others is called:

questions.explanation: Selective permeability means the membrane controls which substances enter or leave.

prompt.text: As volume increases, the surface area to volume ratio __.

questions.explanation: As a cell grows, volume increases faster than surface area, so the SA:V ratio decreases.

prompt.text: The area between the layers of the phospholipid bilayer is:

questions.explanation: Fatty acid tails in the bilayer interior are hydrophobic and nonpolar.

prompt.text: Other molecules in/on the phospholipid bilayer include:

questions.explanation: Membranes commonly include cholesterol and proteins (and often carbohydrates on the outer surface).

prompt.text: Where are rRNA and ribosomes synthesized?

questions.explanation: The nucleolus is the site of rRNA synthesis and ribosome subunit assembly.

prompt.text: The function of ribosomes is:

questions.explanation: Ribosomes translate mRNA into polypeptides (protein synthesis).

prompt.text: True or false: Ribosomes are fixed in place.

questions.explanation: Ribosomes can be free in the cytosol or bound to rough ER; they are not permanently fixed.

prompt.text: Unlike the rough ER, the smooth ER

questions.explanation: Smooth ER synthesizes lipids and detoxifies; rough ER is studded with ribosomes for protein synthesis.

prompt.text: The Golgi Apparatus is responsible for:

questions.explanation: The Golgi modifies, sorts, packages, and ships proteins and lipids.

prompt.text: Lysosomes are responsible for digesting:

questions.explanation: Lysosomes digest macromolecules and damaged material, including engulfed bacteria and cellular components during autophagy.

prompt.text: Vacuoles in plant cells are primarily responsible for:

questions.explanation: The large central vacuole in plant cells mainly stores water, ions, and other materials and maintains turgor.

prompt.text: The most well-documented role of peroxisomes is:

questions.explanation: Peroxisomes transfer hydrogen to O2, forming H2O2, and help break down fatty acids/toxins.

prompt.text: True or false: Plant cells contain both mitochondria and chloroplasts.

questions.explanation: Plant cells have mitochondria for respiration and chloroplasts for photosynthesis.

prompt.text: True or false: Mitochondria have their own separate DNA.

questions.explanation: Mitochondria have their own circular DNA and ribosomes, consistent with bacterial ancestry.

prompt.text: The presence of mitochondria in eukaryotic cells supports the theory of:

questions.explanation: Endosymbiosis explains mitochondria (and chloroplasts) as formerly free-living prokaryotes.

prompt.text: Order the cytoskeletal elements from thinnest to thickest.

questions.explanation: Diameter order: microfilaments (actin) < intermediate filaments < microtubules.

prompt.text: The ECM does not directly provide which of the following:

questions.explanation: The ECM supports and signals outside the cell; intracellular anchoring is inside the cell.

prompt.text: Which of the following is not an animal cell junction?

questions.explanation: Plasmodesmata are plant cell channels. Animal cell junctions include tight junctions, desmosomes, and gap junctions.

prompt.text: Which of the following best matches the cytoskeletal molecules to their function?

options: Microtubules are the “highways”, intermediate filaments are the “girders”, microfilaments are the “locomotive muscles”
Microfilaments are the “highways”, intermediate filaments are the “girders”, microtubules are the “locomotive muscles”
Intermediate filaments are the “highways”, microtubules are the “girders”, microfilaments are the “locomotive muscles”
questions.answer: Microtubules are the “highways”, intermediate filaments are the “girders”, microfilaments are the “locomotive muscles”
questions.explanation: Microtubules track vesicle traffic (“highways”), intermediate filaments provide tensile strength (“girders”), and microfilaments enable contractile movement (“muscles”).
